The tools at your disposal are clear, and it's up to you to figure out how to apply them. However, lines are frequently stilted and confusing, and the voice actors struggle to make the best of what they're given. This makes OSINT and social engineering (the game's two main features) more difficult than they need to be. I can't recommend playing yet. Better translation and voice direction would go a long way to improving future versions.

So, I got this game because it reminded me a lot of Orwell. I've grown to like playing detective games where you learn more about others through their media and all that. And yeah, I know this is a hacking game and different, but it's clear this game was inspired by Orwell, at least to me it was. Now, first going into this, the game was kind of fun. Simple, but fun. It does seem to get harder as you go along and it's interesting to learn more about the chapter your in. 

However, the game has two major problems for me. First off, the interface is a bit annoying. Like, to erase something, you need to actually hit your own delete button. I know this may be nitpicking, but you don't have to do this when copying and pasting, and you are going to be doing a lot of these two. It's also tedious going through the apps. When closing them, for example, you have to recopy  the password in should you need to go back to the same users file. 

Another thing that makes this game a bit annoying for me is the tutorial. This game, unless your good with tech and/or hacking, doesn't do a good job at explaining certain aspects of the game. A good example of this is when you need to hack into someone's phone in chapter two. It's also vaguely explains certain things later in the game and this is done by your jerk of the boss. I don't get this since the beginning had a pretty nice tutorial. 

I don't want to say it's a bad game. It's not actually. But honestly, the interface and lacking tutorial for later and important parts of the game make this not fun for me. If you're someone who doesn't care much for these things or good with tech/hacking,  I'll think you'll enjoy it. The game is lacking a bit though in terms of really getting into these peoples' life and getting to know them. I wish it had done more of that because the chapters are interesting. Still, I'll change my review should these two things be changed (or at least the interface.) It's not a bad game and is decent, but for me at the moment I don't want to keep playing it.

review_text_raw:
This game had a solid idea, but the execution is a complete disaster. The UI is an absolute nightmare—it feels less like you're playing and more like you're struggling to get it to work as you intended. Instead of immersing you, it just makes you want to slam your head into a brick wall. You're endlessly clicking, hoping for something to highlight and when it finally does? It’s barely relevant to the information you want t look for.

And the worst part? The game presents obvious clues in fragmented parts, but it doesn’t let you connect them until it decides you’ve "earned it". You can see the bigger picture, but it keeps those pieces hidden, forcing you to waste time hunting for stuff that’s already right in front of you. It’s like the game is deliberately holding back info, making you run in circles just to unlock something that should’ve been obvious from the start.

To top it all off, you can’t even explore anything the game doesn’t deem necessary, no matter how much you know it should be. Even when you’re certain something else is important, the game stops you, forcing you to stick to its narrow path. It’s like being told exactly where to stand and when to look, even though you can see a whole branch of information that just "not related" .

Is this just me being picky about how the game should be or should I try to give it another shot?

I'd recommend anyone who's interested in playing it to wait until it's out of early access when some of the issues has hopefully been ironed out.

Good: 
- The game's story and art is good.
- Decent interface (well coded).

Bad: 
- Puzzles often have unrealistic time limits or forces you to guess the answer, and after the time runs  or you guess wrong you have to rewatch all of the dialogue before the puzzle started.
- Evidence often don't make sense, things that seem irrelevant are often evidence and vice versa.
- Plenty of spelling mistakes.
- The 5th chapter can't be completed at the moment due to a bug,
- The game doesn't reward you for thinking on your own when collecting evidence or hacking people (with a few exceptions).
- There isn't really a difficulty curve and the game never really opens up in terms of gameplay.

The mechanics are that of an uninspired phishing simulation. Which contrasts with the narrative framing of "you are a really dangerous nerd". I feel like a game like grayhack or hacknet is fit more for that framing. Even the tutorial was highly boring for me. Maybe the story you get after the tutorial is good, but i didn't get that far.

Well you see I understand that a game would need some embellishing and effects to sell the power fantasy and divert from the seams of skipping real life logic, but the choices this game made regarding that front makes me see those seams harder rather than immersing me in the fantasy.

very light spoilers ahead from the first ten minutes of gameplay(tutorial and intro)

First, i got whiplashed right off with the phrase "our company got a BILLION BYTES of customer data". Holy shit dude, that's a lot for a large tech company at the like 90s maybe. Not for the presented "everyone is glued to their phones using social media" setting.  Less than a god damn gigabyte, basically three times less than the space this game takes on your ssd.

Then we got the random code prompts opening every time we copy the details from the browser about someone's facebook account to some contacts type information collection software. It feels less hackery and more like the "linux users when x" memes, because why would code prompts open when you are just copy pasting something from one gui to some other gui.


Then apparently we have access to the data of almost all citizens in our nation through the company database software. For some reason when accessing the data we or the software executes almost totally unrelated linux commands, which i don't understand why since it is not a cli tool but poses as a professional corpo gui software, but i guess the company in the story fired the user interface designer/programmer before they finished their job.

Then there is the password "cracker" software. Except this game's version makes me feel like a loser script kiddie the most. All you do is fill in a bunch of details you gathered from the dude's social media page, and the "cracker" spits out some password guess with very few amount of characters based on the entered information. And somehow it's correct like it's some oracle.

It reminds me of that one CheeseParade skit where the guy goes "He's not a hacker, he's a password guesser", and then the guy proceeds to get locked out of the system for inputting the wrong password since it was a guess based on a whim.

Also the OS apparently can't handle a bunch of high speed showcase of cyber security news, crashes and has to restart, which felt like a funny unintentional commentary on the ram shortage crisis. That was the most fun part of the game for me. 

Anyways, so if you like an overly dressed up phishing simulator with seemingly nice worldbuilding and perhaps a good story if you ignore the technical knowledge shortcomings of the writers here and there, maybe its your thing, Otherwise, nah.

Really wish I could recommend this game but the bugs and poor translation ruin what would have otherwise been a cool experience. Ran into two game breaking bugs, one fixed after a reset and the other remains to be fixed, in the last chapter. After solving a puzzle the game reverts back to a state before the puzzle was solved, while the timer continues to countdown.

Another huge problem, especially in the last chapter, is the game is throwing a ton of background lore at you while an onscreen timer ticks away, in a scenario where the game can't even be paused. The interface already makes it hard to quickly grab information, but now you have to grab it while racing the clock, and solving puzzles. Your option is either to go slow and actually absorb the lore (failing and having to repeat after multiple attempts), or go quickly and miss anything story related. 

The concept of this game is great and almost done well here. ALMOST. It needs better translation and better writing, way less bugs and a better UI. Whether it was script or direction, the voice acting was not up to par either.

Playing for so long only for the game to break at the end really soured me on it, but I'm hoping the devs can fix it for their next iteration, because there is definite potential here.

review_text_raw:
TL;DR: What it lacks in interesting mechanics it makes up for in repetetiveness.

Slightly longer review: 

You google names, go to their facebook page, click on interesting info and then google that, or enter it into the same five programs while the UI makes you wait for 10 seconds every time you found a hint. Then you answer some exams to check if you paid attention. If you expect deductions or logic puzzles, you will not find those here. It is all simply about reading and remembering information.

Sometimes there are minigames but they are also not interesting. One in particular really sucks, because you simply aren't given the information necessary to make the correct decisions, so you just click on random stuff until it somehow works.

It is one of those games where I suffered through the last 3 hours because I wanted to see the ending, but I had my head in my hands a couple times because it was just so annoying sometimes.

The writing.. well first of all, from a purely technical standpoint, it is bad. Clearly whoever wrote this is not fluent in english. There are tons of typos and grammatical errors all over the place. Things which could have easily been fixed by proofreading. Funnily, it gets better torwards the end. Or I just stopped paying attention, which is probably more likely.

From a stroy perspective, it is actually *ok*. Not great, not terrible. There were definitely some good parts, some twists, and some hateable characters. The main issue is that the gameplay is so boring that torwards the end you just use your mouse to scan over text really quickly to find hints, and stop actually reading it.

Overall score: meh/5.

review_text_raw:
I rarely post negative reviews cause I usually pick the games I buy very carefully. I was looking for a fun hacking game though and with the limited selection out there I chose this based on its "Very positive" user reviews. I was actually going to give it a thumbs up too, until I actually read the question Steam asks:
"Would you recommend this game to other players".
To that specific question I would definitely have to say: No.
It's tough, cause I kinda like the game, I just wouldn't expect other players or a friend to have the amount of patience with it that I've had. Subjectively, I'd score it a 7/10, objectively I'd give it a 4/10.

TL;DR The game sets you up for failure. Timers on puzzles mean replaying sections where you fail to solve the puzzle on time, which in some cases are virtually impossible to do on your first try. Then short cutting the info gathering to buy time on your next try, because you already have the info in your head, sometimes introduces game breaking bugs. All this also pushes the player towards walkthroughs completely ruining the experience. Game also has some immersion breaking unnatural language issues.

PROS:
- Interesting story with some good twists.
- Immersive. You can really get into following along with the stories of the people you "hack" and the hacking makes you feel empowered.
- Valuable message around personal data, AI and social media in general.
- A few fun, innovative puzzles.
- Well made UI and visuals (Nothing special, but not bad)

CONS:
- Convoluted puzzles. Some puzzles require you to assume things that aren't intuitive. Like having to use concatenated dates as a password but not being told that specific parts of the dates need to be left out. Having these on a timer seriously exasperates the problem.
- Language issues. Whoever wrote the script and content for this game is definitely not a natural English speaker. All the spelling is correct but the grammar is flawed and the manner of speaking is jarringly foreign. Like everything was written in Japanese and then run through Google translate or something. Unnecessary extra words in places and weird grammar immediately make you feel like "This is not the way people speak". It's honestly quite immersion breaking in a game that involves a lot of reading.
- One or two bugs. Mostly the game runs just fine, in fact you could pretty much run it on a potato. I literally only encountered one bug, but it was game breaking and required that I reload which lost me some progress. The biggest issue about it is that it was caused by trying to short cut problems with the first con I mentioned meaning that alleviating the biggest issue of the game isn't an option.

I appreciate the idea they tried to execute on, but unfortunately the execution is a bit of a mess. I think my main problem is that case facts are slowly fed to you, and you're not allowed to have any leaps of intuition -- you have to follow the preset path that the developers envisioned.

The UI is also a bit of a mess. There's so many different hacking tools that were added to give you the feeling that you're actually "hacking," but it boils down to copy-pasting data into different forms.

Coming from other puzzle games in the same vein, I'm sad that this game misses the mark.
